title: AV nodal reentrant tachycardia (AVNRT)
summary: Two pathways in the AV node form a circuit: down the slow pathway, back up the fast one.

events.label: Sinus beat
events.caption: In sinus rhythm the impulse reaches the AV node by two routes, a fast pathway and a slow pathway. It takes the fast one, which is the AV node route shown in yellow.
events.ecg: A normal P wave, PR interval and narrow QRS.

events.label: Premature atrial beat
events.caption: A premature atrial beat arrives early, while the fast pathway is still refractory. The fast pathway has the longer refractory period.

events.label: Down the slow pathway
events.caption: Blocked in the fast pathway, the impulse goes down the slow pathway, which recovers quickly. It conducts slowly.
events.ecg: The PR interval is long: the impulse is crawling down the slow pathway.

events.label: Reaches the His bundle
events.caption: At the lower end of the pathways the impulse enters the His bundle and the ventricles, and also turns back up the fast pathway, which has now recovered.

events.label: Back up the fast pathway
events.caption: The impulse reaches the atria again through the fast pathway: an atrial echo. It can re-enter the slow pathway, and the circuit is established.
events.ecg: A retrograde P wave, buried in or just after the QRS.

events.label: Tachycardia
events.caption: Round and round: down the slow pathway, up the fast pathway. Atria and ventricles are activated almost together, at about 180 per minute.
events.ecg: A regular narrow-complex tachycardia in which the P wave is hidden in the QRS (a small notch at its end).

teaching_points: AVNRT uses two pathways in the AV node: a fast one with a long refractory period and a slow one with a short refractory period (slides 50-52).
Sinus beats take the fast pathway; a premature atrial beat blocks in the fast pathway, goes down the slow one and returns by the fast one (slide 53).
Atria and ventricles are activated simultaneously, so the P wave is hidden in or just after the QRS (slide 55).
The slow pathway is the usual ablation target.
